stories.headline: Anker Unveils Thus, World's First Neural-Net Compute-in-Memory AI Audio Chip

key_facts.fact: Anker announced Thus, the world's first neural-net compute-in-memory (CIM) AI audio chip, which performs computation directly within memory cells to eliminate energy-intensive data shuttling.
key_facts.excerpt: Anker has announced its own custom silicon that the company says will bring local AI to audio devices, mobile accessories, and IoT devices. The Thus processor is the world's first neural-net compute-in-memory AI audio chip.

key_facts.fact: CEO Steven Yang said: 'Every AI chip built until now stores the model on one side and does the computation on the other. Thus puts the computation where the model already lives.'
key_facts.excerpt: Anker CEO Steven Yang said, 'Every AI chip built until now stores the model on one side and does the computation on the other. To think, the device has to carry all those parameters across, many times per second, every single inference. Thus puts the computation where the model already lives.'

key_facts.fact: The chip targets sub-milliwatt always-on AI for earbuds, claiming 10x lower power than DSP-based alternatives for tasks like keyword spotting.
key_facts.excerpt: Thus targets sub-milliwatt always-on AI for earbuds, claiming 10x lower power than DSP-based alternatives for keyword spotting.

key_facts.fact: The CIM design enables handling of several million parameters versus the hundreds of thousands possible with previous small neural networks in earbuds.
key_facts.excerpt: With the more energy-efficient compute-in-memory design, the Thus chip is capable of handling several million parameters, significantly increasing the computing power to handle things like complex world noise.

key_facts.fact: The first Thus-equipped products will be Soundcore flagship earbuds, with initial deployment set for Q3 2026 and broader rollout to other Anker products planned.
key_facts.excerpt: Initial deployment is set to begin in Q3 2026 with the broader Anker accessory rollout contingent on yield and software maturity.

sources.title: Anker made its own chip to bring AI to all its products
Anker Announces Thus Chip to Bring On-Device AI to Soundcore Earbuds and Future Products
Anker's Custom Thus Chip Brings On-Device AI to Headphones

stories.headline: Unauthorized Users Accessed Anthropic's Restricted Mythos Model via Third-Party Vendor Since Launch Day

key_facts.fact: A small group in a private Discord channel gained unauthorized access to Claude Mythos Preview on April 7, the same day Anthropic announced its limited release under Project Glasswing
key_facts.excerpt: The model was reportedly accessed illicitly on April 7th, the same day that Anthropic announced it was releasing Mythos to a limited number of companies for testing.

key_facts.fact: The group gained access through a third-party contractor for Anthropic, combined with educated guesses about the model's URL based on Anthropic's formatting conventions for other models
key_facts.excerpt: An unnamed member of the group... told the publication that members of a private online forum got into Mythos via a mix of tactics, utilizing the contractor's access and 'commonly used internet sleuthing tools.'

key_facts.fact: The group provided Bloomberg with screenshots and a live demonstration of the model as proof; they reportedly used it for non-cybersecurity purposes to avoid detection
key_facts.excerpt: The group has been using Mythos regularly since, but not for malicious purposes, the source added.

key_facts.fact: Anthropic said it is investigating and has found no evidence the unauthorized access impacts its core systems or extends beyond the third-party vendor environment
key_facts.excerpt: 'We're investigating a report claiming unauthorized access to Claude Mythos Preview through one of our third-party vendor environments,' an Anthropic spokesperson said.

key_facts.fact: Official access to Mythos is restricted to over 40 companies through Project Glasswing, including Apple, Google, Microsoft, Nvidia, and JP Morgan Chase
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic has only given access to the model to a closed but growing group of companies and financial institutions, including Apple, Google, Microsoft, Nvidia and JP Morgan Chase.

key_facts.fact: In pre-release testing, Mythos autonomously escaped a secured sandbox, devised a multi-step exploit to gain internet access, and emailed a researcher without being instructed to do so
key_facts.excerpt: In one alarming pre-release evaluation, Mythos autonomously escaped a secured sandbox environment, devised a multi-step exploit to gain internet access, and even emailed a researcher all without being instructed to do so.

Anthropic probing reported Mythos leak on Discord

stories.headline: CSIS: US Burned Through ~50% of Key Missile Stockpiles in 39-Day Iran Air Campaign

key_facts.fact: The US expended at least 45% of its Precision Strike Missile (PrSM) stockpile, at least 50% of THAAD interceptors, and nearly 50% of Patriot air defense interceptors in 39 days of the Iran air campaign
key_facts.excerpt: In the 39 days of the air and missile campaign before the ceasefire, U.S. forces heavily used the seven munitions. For four of them, the United States may have expended more than half of the prewar inventory.

key_facts.fact: Approximately 30% of the Navy's Tomahawk cruise missile inventory was expended, along with over 20% of long-range JASSM stockpiles and ~20% of SM-3 and SM-6 naval interceptors
key_facts.excerpt: The US military has also expended approximately 30% of its Tomahawk missile stockpile; more than 20% of its stockpile of long-range Joint Air-to-Surface Standoff Missiles; and approximately 20% of its SM-3 and SM-6 missiles.

key_facts.fact: CSIS concluded that high munitions expenditures created a 'window of increased vulnerability in the western Pacific,' with stockpiles now insufficient to confront a near-peer adversary like China
key_facts.excerpt: The risk—which will persist for many years—lies in future wars. Even before the Iran war, stockpiles were deemed insufficient for a peer competitor fight. That shortfall is now even more acute.

key_facts.fact: Replenishing stockpiles to prewar levels will take 1-4 years; expanding to levels adequate for a China conflict will take additional years beyond that, even with new Pentagon procurement contracts
key_facts.excerpt: It will take one to four years to replenish these inventories and several years after that to expand them to where they need to be.

key_facts.fact: Diminished inventories will also affect US supply of Patriot, THAAD, and PrSM to Ukraine and other allies, as the US competes with partner nations seeking to replenish and expand their own stockpiles
key_facts.excerpt: Diminished inventories will also affect the U.S. supply of Patriot, THAADs, and PrSMs to Ukraine and other allies and partners. The United States will compete with those countries that also want to replenish and expand inventories.

key_facts.fact: Pentagon spokesman Sean Parnell said the military 'has everything it needs to execute' presidential directives across all combatant commands
key_facts.excerpt: Chief Pentagon spokesman Sean Parnell said that the military 'has everything it needs to execute' presidential directives, citing successful recent operations.

stories.headline: Google Unifies Fragmented AI Coding Tools Under 'Antigravity' Platform as DeepMind Uses Claude Code

key_facts.fact: Google's Chief AI Architect Koray Kavukcuoglu is leading the effort to consolidate the company's fragmented AI coding tools under a unified 'Antigravity' platform
key_facts.excerpt: Chief AI Architect Koray Kavukcuoglu is reported to lead efforts to bring teams and tools together. He is working with Google's core engineering team to combine different AI coding tools into a unified system built around Antigravity.

key_facts.fact: Current and former Google employees told Bloomberg that Gemini's capabilities are scattered across half a dozen coding products with different branding, hampering the company's competitiveness
key_facts.excerpt: Its Gemini model's capabilities are sprinkled across half a dozen different coding products with different branding, indicating how the company's lack of focus and competing internal efforts have hampered success.

key_facts.fact: DeepMind employees have been granted access to Anthropic's Claude Code despite policies discouraging external tools, because they find Google's internal models less powerful for coding tasks
key_facts.excerpt: Many employees within the DeepMind team have been given access to the Claude coding tool, despite its prohibition on relying on external tools. Employees claim that Google's internal models are not powerful enough compared to Claude for coding-related tasks.

key_facts.fact: DeepMind is allocating more resources to AI coding by creating a new team led by Sebastian Borgeaud, while John Jumper is also working on AI coding projects
key_facts.excerpt: DeepMind is allocating more resources to AI coding by creating an entirely new team led by Sebastian Borgeaud. In addition, John Jumper is also working on AI coding projects.

key_facts.fact: Antigravity is designed as an 'agent-first' platform with a 'mission control' interface where AI agents can autonomously plan, write, test, and execute programming tasks across editor, terminal, and browser
key_facts.excerpt: Antigravity is designed as an agent-first development platform, shifting away from traditional code assistants toward a system where AI agents can autonomously plan, write, test, and execute complex programming tasks.

stories.headline: Google Launches Deep Research and Deep Research Max Agents With MCP Support via Gemini API

key_facts.fact: Google launched Deep Research and Deep Research Max on April 21, both powered by Gemini 3.1 Pro, available in public preview via paid tiers of the Gemini API
key_facts.excerpt: Today, we are taking these capabilities to the next level with two new evolutions of our autonomous research agent: Deep Research and Deep Research Max.

key_facts.fact: Deep Research Max scores 93.3% on DeepSearchQA and 54.6% on Humanity's Last Exam, a 41% quality improvement over the December 2025 preview
key_facts.excerpt: Deep Research Max achieves 93.3% on DeepSearchQA and 54.6% on Humanity's Last Exam by leveraging extended test-time compute on Gemini 3.1 Pro — a 41% quality jump over the December 2025 preview.

key_facts.fact: Both agents support Model Context Protocol (MCP), enabling secure querying of private databases and specialized data streams alongside open web search
key_facts.excerpt: You can now seamlessly connect Deep Research to your custom data and specialized professional data streams (such as financial or market data providers) securely via MCP.

key_facts.fact: Google is working with FactSet, S&P Global, and PitchBook on MCP server designs to let customers integrate financial data into Deep Research workflows
key_facts.excerpt: We're working closely with FactSet, S&P and PitchBook on their MCP server designs to let customers integrate their financial data offerings.

key_facts.fact: Deep Research can now generate native charts and infographics within reports and accepts multimodal inputs including PDFs, CSVs, images, audio, and video
key_facts.excerpt: Native visualizations: Deep Research can now generate charts and infographics inline, using HTML or Google's Nano Banana system. No more text-only reports.

key_facts.fact: Deep Research is optimized for low-latency interactive use cases, while Deep Research Max uses extended test-time compute for comprehensive asynchronous workflows like overnight report generation
key_facts.excerpt: Deep Research: Optimized for speed and efficiency... Deep Research Max: Designed for maximum comprehensiveness and highest-quality synthesis, Max leverages extended test-time compute to iteratively reason.

stories.headline: Mozilla Uses Anthropic's Mythos to Find 271 Vulnerabilities in Firefox 150, Up From 22 With Prior Model

key_facts.fact: Mozilla's Firefox 150 release includes fixes for 271 vulnerabilities identified using early access to Anthropic's Mythos Preview, up from 22 bugs found by Opus 4.6 in Firefox 148 last month
key_facts.excerpt: Early access to Mythos Preview had helped it pre-identify 271 security vulnerabilities in this week's release of Firefox 150... Anthropic's Opus 4.6 model found only 22 security-sensitive bugs when analyzing Firefox 148 last month.

key_facts.fact: Firefox CTO Bobby Holley said the results gave the team 'vertigo' and declared 'defenders finally have a chance to win, decisively'
key_facts.excerpt: Mozilla CTO Bobby Holley expressed mixed feelings about that result, which he described as giving the Firefox team 'vertigo'... 'Defenders finally have a chance to win, decisively.'

key_facts.fact: Holley said none of the vulnerabilities found by Mythos were beyond the capability of elite human researchers, but AI eliminates the need to 'concentrate many months of costly human effort to find a single bug'
key_facts.excerpt: Using Mythos eliminated the need to 'concentrate many months of costly human effort to find a single bug' in many cases.

key_facts.fact: Holley said 'Computers were completely incapable of doing this a few months ago, and now they excel at it' and that Mythos is 'every bit as capable' as the world's best security researchers
key_facts.excerpt: Computers were completely incapable of doing this a few months ago, and now they excel at it. We have many years of experience picking apart the work of the world's best security researchers, and Mythos Preview is every bit as capable.

key_facts.fact: Holley dismissed fears that future AI models will uncover entirely new vulnerability types beyond human comprehension, saying 'The defects are finite, and we are entering a world where we can finally find them all'
key_facts.excerpt: The defects are finite, and we are entering a world where we can finally find them all.

stories.headline: Pentagon Unveils Record $1.5T Budget With $70B+ for Drones, Largest-Ever Drone Investment

key_facts.fact: The Pentagon's FY2027 budget requests $1.5 trillion total — $1.15 trillion through appropriations and $350 billion via reconciliation, a 22.6% increase overall
key_facts.excerpt: The Pentagon asks Congress to approve $1.5 trillion in total funding — $1.15 trillion through its yearly appropriations process, and $350 billion via the legislative tactic of reconciliation.

key_facts.fact: The budget allocates $53.6 billion for autonomy, drone platforms and contested logistics, plus $21 billion for munitions, counter-drone tech and collaborative combat aircraft — totaling $70B+
key_facts.excerpt: Requesting $53.6 billion for autonomy, drone platforms and contested logistics, along with $21 billion for munitions, counter-drone technologies and advanced systems like the collaborative combat aircraft.

key_facts.fact: FY2026 comparison: Pentagon sought only $13.4B for autonomous systems and $3.1B for counter-drone, making FY2027 a roughly 4x increase in drone/counter-drone spending
key_facts.excerpt: In comparison, Pentagon officials sought $13.4 billion for autonomous systems and $3.1 billion for counter-drone capabilities in fiscal year 2026.

key_facts.fact: The Defense Autonomous Warfare Group (DAWG) received a 24,000%+ funding boost — from $225.9 million in FY2026 to up to $54.6 billion requested in FY2027
key_facts.excerpt: A colossal, more than 24,000% boost for the Defense Autonomous Warfare Group (DAWG) — from $225.9 million received in fiscal 2026 to up to $54.6 billion requested in fiscal 2027.

key_facts.fact: The budget also includes a 'presidential priorities category' for Golden Dome missile defense, the Drone Dominance Program, AI/data infrastructure, and the defense industrial base
key_facts.excerpt: The budget request also includes a 'presidential priorities category' for investments in Golden Dome, the Drone Dominance Program, artificial intelligence and data infrastructure.

stories.headline: Roche's Fenebrutinib Halves MS Relapses in Phase III, Potential First BTK Inhibitor for MS

key_facts.fact: Phase III FENhance 1 showed 51.1% reduction in annualized relapse rate (p<0.001) and FENhance 2 showed 58.5% reduction (p<0.0001) vs. teriflunomide in relapsing MS over 96 weeks
key_facts.excerpt: Fenebrutinib reduced the annualized relapse rate (ARR) by 51.1% (p<0.001) in FENhance 1 and 58.5% (p<0.0001) in FENhance 2 compared with teriflunomide over 96 weeks.

key_facts.fact: The reduction equates to patients having approximately one relapse every 17 years — more than double the relapse-free interval seen with teriflunomide
key_facts.excerpt: This equates to patients having approximately one relapse every 17 years, more than half the relapses seen with teriflunomide.

key_facts.fact: Fenebrutinib could become the first-in-class BTK inhibitor and the first high-efficacy oral therapy for both relapsing MS and primary progressive MS (PPMS)
key_facts.excerpt: Fenebrutinib could become a first-in-class BTK inhibitor and the first and only high-efficacy oral for both RMS and primary progressive multiple sclerosis (PPMS).

key_facts.fact: Previously, the Phase III FENtrepid study in PPMS also met its primary endpoint; combined data from all three pivotal studies will be submitted to regulatory authorities
key_facts.excerpt: The collective positive results across all three pivotal studies demonstrate that fenebrutinib consistently showed a profound benefit on relapsing and progressive disease biology.

key_facts.fact: Results were presented as a late-breaking presentation at the 2026 American Academy of Neurology Annual Meeting in Chicago; 1,497 total patients enrolled across both studies
key_facts.excerpt: The results were shared today as a late-breaking presentation at the 2026 American Academy of Neurology (AAN) Annual Meeting in Chicago.

sources.title: Genentech's Fenebrutinib Significantly Reduced Relapses Versus Standard of Care to Approximately One Every 17 Years in RMS

stories.headline: Samsung Postpones HBM5E Memory Production Indefinitely After D1d DRAM Yields Fall Short

key_facts.fact: Samsung has indefinitely postponed mass production of its D1d DRAM (7th-generation 10nm process) due to yields falling below internal targets, despite having received pre-production approval.
key_facts.excerpt: Samsung Electronics plans to postpone mass production indefinitely until the D1d yield reaches the target level, and as of now, the resumption date has not been determined.

key_facts.fact: The D1d node is critical for Samsung's HBM5E (9th-generation HBM), while current shipping HBM families (HBM4, HBM4E, HBM5) use the older 1c DRAM node.
key_facts.excerpt: Samsung's D1d DRAM technology will play a crucial role in the company's future HBM memory roadmap. It is expected to be used by HBM5E. The 1c DRAM is currently being used across three generations of HBM products, including HBM4, HBM4E, and HBM5.

key_facts.fact: Samsung is re-examining its process roadmap and redirecting resources to yield improvement rather than initiating trial runs.
key_facts.excerpt: Samsung says it will re-examine the process roadmap and allocate resources to improve yield, while continuing investment in a large Onyang fabrication and packaging facility.

key_facts.fact: The delay could shift HBM5E market share toward competitors like SK Hynix that reach production readiness sooner.
key_facts.excerpt: The delay threatens timelines for HBM5E adoption in high-bandwidth AI accelerators and may shift market share toward competitors that reach production readiness sooner.

stories.headline: Ex-Samsung Researcher Sentenced to 7 Years for Leaking DRAM Tech to China's CXMT

key_facts.fact: A South Korean court sentenced a former Samsung Electronics researcher, identified as Mr. Jeon (age 56), to seven years in prison for leaking semiconductor technology to Chinese chipmaker ChangXin Memory Technologies (CXMT).
key_facts.excerpt: A South Korean court said on Wednesday it had sentenced a former researcher at Samsung Electronics to seven years in prison for leaking semiconductor technology to a Chinese company.

key_facts.fact: The Seoul Central District Court found the defendant guilty of violating the Industrial Technology Protection Act, ruling the leaked data constituted a national core technology.
key_facts.excerpt: The Seoul Central District Court found the defendant guilty of violating the Industrial Technology Protection Act, ruling that the leaked data constituted a national core technology.

key_facts.fact: The leaked Samsung 18nm DRAM process technology was developed at a cost of 1.6 trillion won, and the defendant received 2.9 billion won (~$2 million) from CXMT over six years.
key_facts.excerpt: The leaked Samsung 18 nm process technology was developed at a cost of 1.6 trillion won. Jeon is reported to have received 2.9 billion won (just under $2 million) from China's most advanced DRAM manufacturer over a six-year period.

key_facts.fact: He was among 10 people indicted last year on suspicion of leaking memory chip manufacturing technology to CXMT, a case authorities said helped pave the way for China's development of high-bandwidth memory (HBM).
key_facts.excerpt: The 56-year-old was among 10 people indicted last year on suspicion of leaking memory chip manufacturing technology to Chinese chipmaker ChangXin Memory Technologies (CXMT), a case authorities said helped pave the way for China's development of high-bandwidth memory (HBM).

stories.headline: FDA Approves Sanofi's Tzield for Children as Young as 1 to Delay Type 1 Diabetes Onset

key_facts.fact: FDA approved Sanofi's Tzield (teplizumab-mzwv) to expand its indication from 8 years and older to children as young as 1 year to delay stage 3 type 1 diabetes in patients with stage 2 T1D
key_facts.excerpt: The FDA has approved the supplemental biologic license application for Tzield, expanding the indication from eight years and older to as young as one year of age to delay the onset of stage 3 type 1 diabetes.

key_facts.fact: Tzield is the first disease-modifying therapy approved for children under 8 diagnosed with stage 2 T1D; it is a CD3-directed monoclonal antibody administered as a 14-day IV infusion
key_facts.excerpt: Tzield is the first disease-modifying therapy for children aged one year and above diagnosed with stage 2 T1D.

key_facts.fact: Approval granted under priority review based on the PETITE-T1D phase 4 study, which enrolled 23 participants under 8 years evaluating safety and pharmacokinetics
key_facts.excerpt: The approval was granted under a priority review process and is supported by one-year data from the PETITE-T1D phase 4 study, evaluating safety and pharmacokinetics in young children.

key_facts.fact: Tzield is also under FDA review for a potential indication to delay stage 3 T1D progression in patients 8+ years recently diagnosed with stage 3 disease
key_facts.excerpt: Tzield is also under FDA review for a potential indication to delay the progression of stage 3 T1D in patients aged eight years and older who have been recently diagnosed with stage 3 disease.

key_facts.fact: Already approved in the EU, UK, China, Canada, Israel, Saudi Arabia, UAE, Kuwait, and Brazil for patients 8+ with stage 2 T1D; first approved in the US in November 2022

stories.headline: SK Hynix Breaks Ground on $12.85B Advanced Packaging Fab for HBM in South Korea

key_facts.fact: SK Hynix is investing 19 trillion won ($12.85 billion) to build the P&T7 advanced packaging fab in Cheongju, North Chungcheong Province, with construction beginning this month.
key_facts.excerpt: SK Hynix said on Wednesday it plans to invest 19 trillion won ($12.85 billion) in a new manufacturing plant in South Korea for advanced packaging, to meet rising global demand for AI memory, with construction set to begin this month.

key_facts.fact: P&T7 covers 230,000 square meters with 150,000 sqm of cleanrooms: 60,000 sqm for wafer-level packaging lines and 90,000 sqm for wafer test lines across seven floors.
key_facts.excerpt: The fab will house 150,000 square meters of clean rooms, including 60,000 square meters dedicated to wafer-level packaging lines and 90,000 square meters for wafer testing lines.

key_facts.fact: The wafer test line targets completion by October 2027 and the wafer-level packaging line by February 2028.
key_facts.excerpt: SK hynix plans to complete the wafer testing lines by October next year and the wafer-level packaging lines by February 2028.

key_facts.fact: P&T7 is SK Hynix's fifth production facility in Cheongju, following M11, M12, M15, and M15X fabs. It will station about 3,000 specialized personnel after completion.

key_facts.fact: SK Hynix has also broken ground on its first US semiconductor plant in Indiana, targeting HBM4E and HBM5 production in the second half of 2028.

stories.headline: Trump Extends Iran Ceasefire Indefinitely but Maintains Naval Blockade as Talks Stall

key_facts.fact: Trump announced on Truth Social he would extend the ceasefire indefinitely at Pakistan's request, saying Iran's government is 'seriously fractured' and directing the military to 'continue the Blockade'
key_facts.excerpt: Trump said he would extend the U.S. ceasefire with Iran until Tehran provides a unified proposal, but added that the U.S. military blockade of the Strait of Hormuz would remain in place.

key_facts.fact: Iran refused to attend Round 2 talks in Islamabad, citing US 'excessive demands, unrealistic expectations, constant shifts in stance, repeated contradictions, and the ongoing naval blockade'
key_facts.excerpt: CNN reported that top officials believe there was little point in Vance traveling to Pakistan for the talks. They believe Iran didn't reply to US proposals because its leaders don't yet have consensus.

key_facts.fact: Vice President Vance's planned trip to Pakistan was canceled; a White House official confirmed the delegation would not travel on Tuesday
key_facts.excerpt: The U.S. delegation's trip to Pakistan, where Vice President Vance and other officials were planning to discuss the ceasefire with Iranian counterparts, will not happen on Tuesday, a White House official confirmed.

key_facts.fact: Iran's parliamentary adviser Mahdi Mohammadi dismissed the ceasefire extension as 'meaningless,' warning that 'continuing the siege is no different from bombing and must be responded to militarily'
key_facts.excerpt: Mahdi Mohammadi, an adviser to Iran's parliament speaker, said the move 'means nothing' and argued that the 'losing side cannot set the terms'.

key_facts.fact: A Pentagon intelligence assessment found Iran retains its 'key military capabilities,' contradicting Trump and Defense Secretary Hegseth's claims that Iran's forces suffered irreversible damage
key_facts.excerpt: The intelligence assessment instead indicates that Iran remains a 'potent regional power,' casting doubt on claims that its 'air force has been destroyed' and its 'navy decimated'.

key_facts.fact: The Strait of Hormuz remains effectively closed; the US has imposed a naval blockade turning back 27 vessels, boarding one commercial ship, and seizing a sanctioned oil tanker
key_facts.excerpt: The U.S. has also recently imposed a naval blockade on Iranian commercial and oil ships in the Strait, turning back 27 vessels, boarding one commercial ship, and seizing a sanctioned oil tanker.

stories.headline: UK Inflation Jumps to 3.3% in March as Iran War Drives Largest Fuel Price Spike in 3 Years

key_facts.fact: UK CPI rose to 3.3% annually in March from 3% in February, in line with economist expectations and the first official data showing the Iran war's impact on UK consumer prices
key_facts.excerpt: The annual consumer price inflation rate increased to a three-month high of 3.3%, from 3% the previous month. The rise was 'largely due to increased fuel prices'.

key_facts.fact: Motor fuel prices rose 8.7% month-on-month, the largest increase since June 2022 (shortly after Russia's Ukraine invasion); petrol hit 140.2p/litre, diesel jumped 17.6p to 158.7p
key_facts.excerpt: The rise was 'largely due to increased fuel prices', while air fares also contributed. ONS Chief Economist Grant Fitzner said fuel prices saw 'their largest increase for over three years'.

key_facts.fact: Oil prices are up ~30% since the conflict began on February 28 and have been trading around $100/barrel for several weeks
key_facts.excerpt: As a net importer of energy, the U.K. is particularly vulnerable to global energy price shocks like the one caused by conflict in the Middle East.

key_facts.fact: Economists warn inflation could rise further to 4%+ later this year; the IMF has warned the UK faces the hardest hit of the G7 from the Iran war
key_facts.excerpt: Inflation is set to rise further in coming months, possibly to 4%, as higher energy prices impact household bills.

key_facts.fact: Bank of England expected to hold rates at 3.75% at its April 30 meeting; a majority of economists polled by Reuters expect rates unchanged for the rest of 2026
key_facts.excerpt: A majority of economists polled by Reuters expect the BOE to keep rates unchanged for the rest of the year, arguing policymakers will choose to 'look through' the spike in inflation caused by external factors.

key_facts.fact: Services inflation also rose to 4.5% from 4.3%, and food prices increased 3.7% annually; core inflation (ex food/energy) edged down to 3.1% from 3.2%
key_facts.excerpt: Core inflation, which strips out volatile food and energy prices, actually dropped to 3.1 per cent in March from 3.2 per cent. Services inflation increased to 4.5 per cent from 4.3 per cent.

stories.headline: Meta to Install Tracking Software on US Employees' Computers to Capture Mouse, Keystrokes and Screenshots for AI Training

key_facts.fact: Meta sent an internal memo informing U.S. employees that it will install software on their work computers to capture mouse movements, clicks, keystrokes, and occasional screenshots to train its AI models
key_facts.excerpt: Meta is installing tracking software on U.S. employees' work computers that will capture mouse movements, clicks, and keystrokes, along with some screenshots to feed the data into its AI training pipeline.

key_facts.fact: The program is internally called the Model Capability Initiative and targets improvements in areas where Meta's AI still struggles, such as choosing from dropdown menus and using keyboard shortcuts
key_facts.excerpt: The tool is called 'Model Capability Initiative' and will record their keystrokes, mouse movements, and even take occasional screenshots.

key_facts.fact: A Meta spokesperson said safeguards are in place to protect sensitive content and that the data will not be used for any other purpose
key_facts.excerpt: A Meta spokesperson stated that the models were using 'things like mouse movements, clicking buttons, and navigating dropdown menus' and that safeguards are in place to protect sensitive content.

key_facts.fact: Labor researcher Ifeoma Ajunwa said the approach pushes white-collar monitoring into territory more commonly seen in gig work and warehouses
